testcase_name: List all I18N translation groups

testcase_name: Update modules with an invalid boolean value

testcase_name: Add a currency to a pay grade with valid min/max salary
test_objective: Verify a currency can be added to a pay grade with minSalary less than maxSalary, both within allowed range and decimal precision.

3. Enter min salary and max salary (min < max)
expected_results: Currency with min/max salary range is added successfully to the pay grade.

testcase_name: Add a currency with min salary greater than or equal to max salary

test_steps: 1. Navigate to a Pay Grade's Add Currency screen
3. Enter min salary equal to or greater than max salary
expected_results: Error is returned: 'Min salary should be less than max salary'; currency is not added.

testcase_name: Add a currency with min salary of 0
test_objective: Verify minSalary of exactly 0 is treated as a special case and does not trigger the min<max comparison bypass incorrectly.

expected_results: Currency is added successfully with min salary 0.

testcase_name: Add a currency with salary exceeding maximum allowed value

test_steps: 1. Navigate to a Pay Grade's Add Currency screen
expected_results: Validation error is shown for exceeding the maximum allowed salary value; currency is not added.

testcase_name: Add a currency with more than 2 decimal places in salary

expected_results: Validation error is shown for invalid decimal precision; currency is not added.

testcase_name: Add a currency to a non-existent pay grade

testcase_name: Update min/max salary for an existing pay grade currency

test_objective: Verify requesting the job specification for a job title without one returns a not-found error.

test_steps: 1. Send GET request for job specification with a jobTitleId that does not exist
expected_results: A 404 Record Not Found response or validation error is returned.

testcase_name: Punch in successfully with valid date, time and timezone
test_objective: Verify an employee can punch in successfully with all valid required fields.
test_steps: 2. Navigate to Time > Attendance > Punch In/Out
3. Confirm current date, time, timezoneOffset and timezoneName are populated
expected_results: Attendance record is created with state 'PUNCHED IN' and punch-in date/time/timezone are saved correctly.

testcase_name: Punch in fails when date field is missing
test_objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'date' field is not provided.
test_steps: 2. Send Punch In request without 'date' parameter
expected_results: API returns a validation error indicating 'date' is required; no attendance record is created.

testcase_name: Punch in fails when time field is missing
test_objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'time' field is not provided.
test_steps: 2. Send Punch In request without 'time' parameter
expected_results: API returns a validation error indicating 'time' is required; no attendance record is created.

testcase_name: Punch in fails when timezoneOffset is missing
test_objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'timezoneOffset' field is not provided.
test_steps: 2. Send Punch In request without 'timezoneOffset' parameter
expected_results: API returns a validation error for missing timezoneOffset; no attendance record is created.

testcase_name: Punch in fails when timezoneName is missing
test_objective: Verify punch in request is rejected when the required 'timezoneName' field is not provided.
test_steps: 2. Send Punch In request without 'timezoneName' parameter
expected_results: API returns a validation error for missing timezoneName; no attendance record is created.

testcase_name: Punch in fails with invalid time format
test_objective: Verify punch in rejects a time value that does not match the required 'H:i' format.
test_steps: 2. Send Punch In request with time='25:99' (invalid format)
expected_results: API returns a TIME format validation error and no attendance record is created.

testcase_name: Punch in note accepted up to 250 characters
test_objective: Verify the punch-in note field is accepted when it is at the maximum allowed length of 250 characters.
test_steps: 2. Enter a punch-in note of exactly 250 characters
expected_results: Punch in succeeds and the 250-character note is saved without truncation.

testcase_name: Punch in fails when note exceeds 250 characters
test_objective: Verify punch in is rejected when the note field exceeds the 250 character maximum length.

expected_results: API returns a LENGTH validation error for punchInNote/note and no attendance record is created.

testcase_name: Punch in blocked when an overlapping punched-in record already exists
test_objective: Verify punch in is rejected with 'Punch-In Overlap Found' when the employee already has an overlapping open attendance record.
test_steps: 1. Login as ESS user who already has an active punched-in record
2. Attempt to Punch In again with a date/time that overlaps the existing open record
expected_results: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Punch-In Overlap Found'; no new record is created.

testcase_name: Punch in rejected when system time is altered beyond tolerance and 'Allow employees to change time' is disabled
test_objective: Verify punch in fails with 'Provided Date And Time Invalid' when the configuration disallows changing current time and the supplied date/time differs from the actual server time by more than 180 seconds.

3. Submit Punch In with a date/time more than 3 minutes different from the real current time
expected_results: API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Provided Date And Time Invalid'; punch in is rejected.

testcase_name: Punch in succeeds when time is within +/-180 second tolerance and time-change is disabled
test_objective: Verify punch in succeeds when 'Allow employees to change time' is disabled but the supplied date/time is within the 180-second margin of the actual current time.

3. Submit Punch In using the real current date/time (within 3 minutes)
expected_results: Punch in succeeds and attendance record is created with state 'PUNCHED IN'.

testcase_name: Punch in succeeds without an optional note
test_objective: Verify punch in succeeds when the optional 'note' field is left blank.

expected_results: Punch in succeeds and the attendance record is saved with a null/empty note.

testcase_name: Punch out fails when employee has no active punch-in record

testcase_name: Punch out fails when time field is missing

testcase_name: Punch out fails with invalid timezoneOffset value

testcase_name: Punch out succeeds with an optional note within limit

testcase_name: Punch out rejected when system time is altered beyond tolerance and time-change is disabled

test_objective: Verify a work email that fails validation or contains header-injection characters blocks the reset email and routes to the failure page.
test_steps: 1. Configure/target an employee whose work email is malformed or contains a CR/LF header-injection sequence
2. Submit a reset request for that username
expected_results: sendPasswordResetCodeEmail rejects the address via filter_var/regex checks (leading '-' or \r\n), returns false, and RequestResetPasswordController redirects to auth/sendPasswordResetFailure.

testcase_name: Reset request success and failure pages render the correct components
test_objective: Verify the dedicated success and failure landing pages render their respective Vue components.
test_steps: 1. Trigger a successful reset request and observe auth/sendPasswordReset
2. Trigger a failed reset request (e.g. email send failure) and observe auth/sendPasswordResetFailure
expected_results: RequestPasswordSuccessController renders 'reset-password-success'; RequestPasswordFailureController renders 'reset-password-failure'.

testcase_name: Multiple consecutive reset requests for the same user
test_objective: Verify requesting a new reset code before using a previous one is accepted and generates a fresh code (current behaviour, no throttling found in code).
test_steps: 1. Submit a valid reset request for a username
2. Immediately submit a second reset request for the same username
expected_results: Two ResetPasswordRequest rows are created; a new reset code/email is generated each time; no rate limiting or cooldown is enforced in ResetPasswordService/ResetPasswordDao.

testcase_name: Open reset link with a valid, unused, unexpired code
test_objective: Verify a valid reset link renders the reset-password form pre-filled with the correct username.
test_steps: 1. Request a password reset for a valid user
expected_results: ResetPasswordService::validateUrl resolves the user; ResetCodeController renders the 'reset-password' component with username, code, and a 'reset-password' CSRF token.

testcase_name: Submit a new password with a valid code and matching username
test_objective: Verify a user can successfully set a new password through a valid reset link.
test_steps: 2. Enter the matching username and a compliant new password
expected_results: saveResetPassword updates the user's password, updateResetPasswordValid marks the request as used (expired=0), the session is invalidated, and the user is redirected to auth/login.

testcase_name: Open reset link with an invalid/non-existent code
test_objective: Verify a bogus reset code shows an error state rather than a reset form.
expected_results: getResetPasswordLogByResetCode finds no matching request; ResetCodeController renders the 'reset-password-error' component.

testcase_name: Open reset link after it has expired (older than 1 day)
test_objective: Verify a reset code becomes unusable once more than one day has elapsed since it was requested.
test_steps: 2. Wait until hasPasswordResetRequestNotExpired(request) > 0 (more than 1 day elapsed), or manipulate resetRequestDate
expected_results: validateUrl detects the elapsed day count > 0 and returns null; the reset-password-error page is shown.

testcase_name: Reuse an older reset code after a newer one was requested
test_objective: Verify that once a new reset code is requested for the same email, the previous code is no longer accepted (replay of a stale code).
test_steps: 2. Request a second password reset for the same account (code B)
3. Open the link containing code A
expected_results: validateUrl compares code A against the latest stored reset code for that email (code B) via getResetPasswordLogByEmail; since they differ, code A is rejected as 'old one & not valid'.

testcase_name: Reuse a reset code after it has already been used
test_objective: Verify a reset code cannot be used a second time to change the password again.
test_steps: 1. Successfully complete a password reset using a valid code
expected_results: updateResetPasswordValid already set expired=0 for that email; validateUrl's !$resetPassword->getExpired() check now evaluates true, so the code is treated as expired/invalid and rejected.

testcase_name: Submit reset password with a username that does not match the reset code owner
test_objective: Verify the reset form rejects a username that does not belong to the resolved reset code.
test_steps: 1. Open a valid reset link for user A
2. Edit/submit the form with a different username, e.g. user B
expected_results: ResetPasswordController compares $user->getUserName() to the submitted username; on mismatch it throws AuthenticationException::invalidResetCode.

testcase_name: Submit reset password form with missing or invalid CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the reset-password form enforces CSRF protection.
test_steps: 2. Submit the form with the _token field removed or altered
expected_results: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('reset-password', token) fails; AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken is thrown before the password is changed.

testcase_name: Submit a weak/non-compliant new password via reset password form
test_objective: Verify whether the reset-password flow enforces the configured password strength policy before saving (documents current behaviour/possible gap).
test_steps: 2. Enter a very short/weak password (e.g. '1234') as the new password
expected_results: ResetPasswordController::handle calls saveResetPassword directly with no PasswordStrengthService/PasswordStrengthValidation check in this controller; verify whether the weak password is accepted (current code path does not call the strength validator here) - flag as a gap if it is accepted.

testcase_name: Successful password reset invalidates the current session
test_objective: Verify that completing a reset forces any existing session to end, requiring fresh login with the new password.
test_steps: 1. While logged in on Browser A, complete a password reset for the same account on Browser B
expected_results: ResetPasswordController::handle calls $session->invalidate() after saving the new password; Browser A's session is no longer valid on the next request.

testcase_name: Login succeeds but password fails the strength policy while enforcement is on
test_objective: Verify a technically-correct login is intercepted and redirected to forced password reset when the password does not meet the configured strength policy.
test_steps: 2. Log in with correct credentials for a password that fails isValidPassword()
expected_results: LocalAuthProvider throws PasswordEnforceException, invalidates the session, generates an enforce-password reset code, and ValidateController redirects to changeWeakPassword/resetCode/{code} instead of the home page.

testcase_name: Weak password reset page loads with a valid reset code
test_objective: Verify the forced reset page correctly identifies the user and renders the change-password form.
test_steps: 1. Trigger the weak-password flow to obtain a reset code
expected_results: PasswordStrengthService::validateUrl returns true; WeakPasswordResetController renders 'reset-weak-password' with username, code, and a 'reset-weak-password' CSRF token.

testcase_name: Weak password reset page with an invalid or already-used code
test_objective: Verify an invalid enforce-password reset code shows the invalid-code state rather than the form.
expected_results: validateUrl returns false (no matching record or isExpired()=true); the component receives invalid-code=true and does not expose the change-password fields.

testcase_name: Enforce-password reset code expires after 1 hour
test_objective: Verify an enforce-password reset code becomes invalid once more than one hour has passed since the request.
test_steps: 1. Trigger the weak-password flow to obtain a reset code
2. Wait over 1 hour (or adjust resetRequestDate) so dateDiffInHours > 1
expected_results: isResetCodeTimeOut returns true; validateUrl marks the request updateEnforcedPasswordValid(...,true) and returns false, showing the invalid-code state.

testcase_name: Submit a strong new password with the correct current password
test_objective: Verify a user can successfully replace a weak password with a compliant one via the forced-reset form.
test_steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link
3. Enter a new password meeting all policy rules
expected_results: isCurrentPassword validates the current password, saveEnforcedPassword updates the password and marks the enforce request as used (expired=true), and the user is redirected to auth/login.

testcase_name: Submit the forced-reset form with an incorrect current password
test_objective: Verify the forced-reset flow rejects an incorrect current password.
test_steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link
expected_results: isCurrentPassword returns false; a FLASH_PASSWORD_ENFORCE_ERROR with 'invalid_credentials' is set and the user is redirected back to the same reset page with an error shown.

testcase_name: Submit the forced-reset form with missing/invalid CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the forced password reset form enforces CSRF protection.
test_steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link
2. Submit the form with the _token removed or altered
expected_results: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('reset-weak-password', token) fails; a FLASH_PASSWORD_ENFORCE_ERROR 'invalid_csrf_token' is set and the user is redirected back to the same page.

testcase_name: Submit a new password that still fails the strength policy
test_objective: Verify the forced-reset endpoint blocks a replacement password that still does not satisfy the configured complexity rules.
test_steps: 1. Open a valid weak-password reset link
3. Enter a new password that is still weak (e.g. missing a special character)
expected_results: validateParameters() re-checks isValidPassword() and returns false; RequestResetWeakPasswordController::handleBadRequest() is returned, the password is not saved.

testcase_name: Reuse an enforce-password reset code after it has already been consumed
test_objective: Verify a completed enforce-password reset code cannot be replayed to change the password again.
test_steps: 1. Successfully complete a forced password reset using a code
expected_results: The EnforcePasswordRequest was marked expired=true by updateEnforcedPasswordValid; a subsequent validateUrl call returns false because isExpired() is true.

testcase_name: Username and password field length boundaries on the forced-reset form
test_objective: Verify the forced-reset endpoint enforces username length (5-40 chars) and password max length (64 chars) parameter rules.
test_steps: 1. Submit the forced-reset form with a username of 4 characters (below USERNAME_MIN_LENGTH)
2. Repeat with a password longer than 64 characters (MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH)
expected_results: ParamRuleCollection LENGTH rules fail validation in validateParameters(); the request is rejected via handleBadRequest() rather than being processed.

testcase_name: Password satisfies all configured policy rules
test_objective: Verify a password meeting length, character-class and strength requirements passes validation with no messages.
test_steps: 1. Call POST /api/v2/auth/validation/password (or trigger via reset form) with a password of length >= 8 containing upper, lower, digit, special char, no spaces, and a strong zxcvbn score
expected_results: checkPasswordPolicies returns an empty messages array and isValidPassword returns true; API returns strength score with no warning messages.

testcase_name: Password shorter than the minimum length (7 characters)
test_objective: Verify a password below the configured minimum length (default 8) is flagged.
expected_results: checkMinPasswordLength returns true; the 'auth.password_min_length' message is included and isValidPassword returns false.

testcase_name: Password exactly at the minimum length boundary (8 characters)
test_objective: Verify a password exactly at the configured minimum length is accepted (when all other rules are satisfied).
test_steps: 1. Submit an 8-character password that also satisfies upper/lower/number/special-char/no-space rules
expected_results: checkMinPasswordLength returns false (8 is not < 8); no min-length message is generated.

testcase_name: Password exceeding the maximum length (65 characters)
test_objective: Verify a password longer than MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH (64) is flagged.
expected_results: checkMaxPasswordLength returns true; the 'auth.password_max_length' message is included and isValidPassword returns false.

testcase_name: Password exactly at the maximum length boundary (64 characters)
test_objective: Verify a password exactly at MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH is accepted.
test_steps: 1. Submit a 64-character password satisfying all other rules
expected_results: checkMaxPasswordLength returns false (64 is not > 64); no max-length message is generated.

testcase_name: Password missing an uppercase letter
test_objective: Verify a password with zero uppercase letters is rejected when the policy requires at least one.
test_steps: 1. Submit a password containing only lowercase letters, digits and special characters
expected_results: checkMinUppercaseLetters returns true; the 'auth.password_n_uppercase_letters' message is returned.

testcase_name: Password missing a lowercase letter
test_objective: Verify a password with zero lowercase letters is rejected when the policy requires at least one.
test_steps: 1. Submit a password containing only uppercase letters, digits and special characters
expected_results: checkMinLowercaseLetters returns true; the 'auth.password_n_lowercase_letters' message is returned.

testcase_name: Password missing a numeric digit
test_objective: Verify a password with no digits is rejected when the policy requires at least one number.
test_steps: 1. Submit a password containing only letters and special characters
expected_results: checkMinNumbersInPassword returns true; the 'auth.password_n_numbers' message is returned.

testcase_name: Password missing a special character
test_objective: Verify a password with no special characters is rejected when the policy requires at least one.
test_steps: 1. Submit a password containing only letters and digits
expected_results: checkMinSpecialCharacters returns true; the 'auth.password_n_special_characters' message is returned.

testcase_name: Password containing spaces when spaces are disallowed
test_objective: Verify a password containing whitespace is rejected under the default is_spaces_allowed=false policy.
test_steps: 1. Submit a password containing a space character, e.g. 'Str0ng Pass!'
expected_results: checkSpacesInPassword returns true; the 'auth.password_spaces_not_allowed' message is returned.

testcase_name: Common/guessable password that satisfies character-class rules but has low entropy
test_objective: Verify a predictable password (e.g. 'Password1!') that technically satisfies length/character rules is still flagged as guessable via the zxcvbn strength score.
test_steps: 1. Submit a common/predictable password like 'Password1!' that meets length and character-class rules
2. Inspect the strength score and messages
expected_results: PasswordStrengthValidation::checkPasswordStrength scores it below the configured default_required_password_strength ('strong'); checkRequiredDefaultPasswordStrength returns true and the 'auth.password_could_be_guessable' message is added since no other messages exist.

testcase_name: Login form submitted with a missing CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the login POST is rejected when _token is absent.
test_steps: 1. Submit the login form (ValidateController) with the _token field stripped out
expected_results: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('login', null) returns false; AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken is thrown, caught, and the user is redirected to the login page with an error flash before any credential check occurs.

testcase_name: Login form submitted with an invalid/tampered CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the login POST is rejected when _token does not match the session-issued token.
test_steps: 1. Submit the login form with a random/incorrect _token value and otherwise-valid credentials
expected_results: Token validation fails first; invalid_csrf_token error is shown even though the credentials themselves were correct.

testcase_name: Request-reset-password form missing CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the forgot-password request form is protected against CSRF.
test_steps: 1. Submit the request-reset-password form with _token removed
expected_results: RequestResetPasswordController throws AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken before searching for the user.

testcase_name: Reset-password form missing or invalid CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the final reset-password submission form is protected against CSRF.
test_steps: 1. Submit the reset-password form (valid reset code) with _token removed or altered
expected_results: ResetPasswordController throws AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken before the new password is saved.

testcase_name: Reset-weak-password form missing or invalid CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the forced weak-password reset form is protected against CSRF.
test_steps: 1. Submit the reset-weak-password form with _token removed or altered
expected_results: isValid('reset-weak-password', token) fails; a FLASH_PASSWORD_ENFORCE_ERROR invalid_csrf_token is set and the user is redirected back without the password being changed.

testcase_name: Administrator-access verification form missing or invalid CSRF token
test_objective: Verify the step-up admin verification form is protected against CSRF.
test_steps: 1. Submit the administrator-access verification form with _token removed or altered, using a correct admin password
expected_results: AdministratorVerifyController throws AuthenticationException::invalidCsrfToken even though the password was correct; FLASH_VERIFY_ERROR is set and the user is forwarded back to the verification page.

testcase_name: Token issued for one form cannot validate a different form
test_objective: Verify each form uses a distinct CSRF token namespace (id) so a token cannot be replayed across unrelated forms.
test_steps: 1. Capture the CSRF token rendered on the login page ('login' id)
2. Attempt to submit the reset-password form using that token value as _token
expected_results: CsrfTokenManager::isValid('reset-password', loginToken) returns false because the token id differs, so validation fails.

testcase_name: A fresh, unique CSRF token is issued on every relevant page load
test_objective: Verify token freshness/uniqueness so tokens are not trivially predictable or globally shared.
test_steps: 1. Load the login page twice in separate sessions
expected_results: Each session receives its own token value bound to that session's TokenStorage, per Symfony CsrfTokenManager semantics.

testcase_name: Expired session token replay after logout
test_objective: Verify a CSRF token captured before logout cannot be used to perform a state-changing action after the session ends.
test_steps: 1. Log in and capture the login page's CSRF token
3. Attempt to submit an authenticated form action using the captured token
expected_results: Because the session/token storage was invalidated on logout, the previously captured token no longer validates against the new session state.

testcase_name: User without admin-verify permission is forwarded to Forbidden page
test_objective: Verify a user lacking the 'auth_admin_verify' data-group read permission cannot reach the admin verification step.
test_steps: 1. Log in as a user/role without permission on data group 'auth_admin_verify'
2. Trigger an action that invokes AdministratorVerifyController
expected_results: getDataGroupPermissions('auth_admin_verify')->canRead() is false; a RequestForwardableException forwards the request to ForbiddenController, rendering the 403 'auth-forbidden' page.

testcase_name: Authorized admin submits correct password on the verification page
test_objective: Verify a permitted user can step up to admin access by re-entering their password correctly.
test_steps: 1. Navigate to an admin-privileged action, triggering the Administrator Access page
expected_results: AuthenticationService::setCredentials succeeds; AuthUser::setHasAdminAccess(true) is set, the login is logged, and the user is forwarded to the originally requested (forward) URL.

testcase_name: Authorized admin submits an incorrect password on the verification page
test_objective: Verify re-authentication fails safely when the wrong password is supplied on the step-up form.
test_steps: 1. Navigate to the Administrator Access page
expected_results: setCredentials returns false, AuthenticationException::invalidCredentials is thrown, FLASH_VERIFY_ERROR is set, and the user is forwarded back to AdministratorAccessController with the error shown; hasAdminAccess remains false.

testcase_name: Admin access flag is not sticky across page navigation
test_objective: Verify that gaining admin access on one page does not silently grant it on subsequent unrelated pages, per AdministratorAccessSubscriber.
test_steps: 1. Successfully verify admin access for one privileged action
2. Navigate to a different Vue-rendered controller that does not implement AdminPrivilegeController
expected_results: AdministratorAccessSubscriber::onControllerEvent resets AuthUser::setHasAdminAccess(false) for any AbstractVueController that is not an instance of AdminPrivilegeController, forcing re-verification for the next privileged action.

testcase_name: Administrator Access page respects the 'forward' query parameter
test_objective: Verify the intended destination after verification is captured from the 'forward' query string.
expected_results: The forward URL is stored on AuthUser::ADMIN_ACCESS_FORWARD_URL and used to redirect after a successful verification.

testcase_name: Administrator Access page falls back to the home page as the back URL
test_objective: Verify that without an explicit 'back' query parameter (and no prior flash error), the back-url defaults to the user's home page path.
test_steps: 1. Navigate directly to the Administrator Access page with no 'back' query parameter and no pending FLASH_VERIFY_ERROR
expected_results: backUrl is computed as '/' + HomePageService::getHomePagePath() and passed to the component as the 'back-url' prop.

testcase_name: Forward/back session attributes are cleared after successful verification
test_objective: Verify stale forward/back URLs do not leak into subsequent unrelated privileged actions.
test_steps: 1. Successfully complete admin verification with a forward URL set
expected_results: AdministratorVerifyController removes ADMIN_ACCESS_FORWARD_URL and ADMIN_ACCESS_BACK_URL from AuthUser after a successful redirect.

testcase_name: Terminated or disabled admin user cannot pass step-up verification
test_objective: Verify that even with the correct password, a disabled or terminated admin account fails the re-authentication check.
test_steps: 1. As a disabled or terminated admin user with an existing session, trigger the Administrator Access verification
expected_results: AuthenticationService::setCredentialsForUser throws userDisabled/employeeTerminated before hasAdminAccess can be set to true; verification fails.

testcase_name: Forbidden page renders the correct 403 component
test_objective: Verify the Forbidden landing page displays the expected UI when access is denied.
test_steps: 1. Trigger any RequestForwardableException route to ForbiddenController (e.g. lacking admin_verify permission)
expected_results: ForbiddenController::preRender renders the 'auth-forbidden' Vue component with an HTTP 403 status.

testcase_name: Session times out while browsing an authenticated view page
test_objective: Verify an expired/invalidated session on a standard (view) controller redirects the user to the login page instead of showing stale content.
test_steps: 2. Force the session to become unauthenticated (e.g. expire it server-side)
3. Navigate to any authenticated view page
expected_results: AuthenticationSubscriber::onControllerEvent detects the controller is not PublicControllerInterface, throws SessionExpiredException, and onExceptionEvent redirects to auth/login.

testcase_name: Session times out during a REST API call
test_objective: Verify an expired session hitting a REST endpoint returns a structured 401 instead of an HTML redirect.
test_steps: 1. Log in and obtain a session
3. Call any authenticated REST V2 API endpoint
expected_results: AuthenticationSubscriber throws UnauthorizedException carrying an HTTP 401 JSON error body ('Session expired'); onExceptionEvent returns that response directly.

testcase_name: Account is disabled by an admin while the user has an active session
test_objective: Verify a mid-session account disable takes effect on the very next request rather than waiting for re-login.
test_steps: 1. Log in as user X in Session A
2. In a separate admin session, disable user X's account
3. Perform any action in Session A
expected_results: resolveAuthenticatedUserException detects isLoggedInUserActive()=false, logoutCurrentSession invalidates the session and sets a 'user_disabled' flash message; the user is forced back to the login page.

testcase_name: Employee is terminated while the user has an active session
test_objective: Verify a mid-session employee termination immediately revokes access.
test_steps: 1. Log in as user X in an active session
expected_results: resolveAuthenticatedUserException detects the EmployeeTerminationRecord and forces a logout with an 'employee_terminated' message.

testcase_name: User record is modified elsewhere, invalidating the current session token
test_objective: Verify that if the logged-in user's dateModified timestamp changes (e.g. edited by an admin) the current session is treated as stale and ended.
test_steps: 2. Have an admin modify user X's record (changing dateModified)
3. Perform any subsequent action as user X in the original session
expected_results: hasUserLastModifiedChanged returns true; a 'session_expired' AuthenticationException triggers logoutCurrentSession, forcing re-login.

testcase_name: Re-login after session timeout returns the user to the originally requested page
test_objective: Verify the post-timeout login flow restores the user's original destination rather than always going to the home page.
test_steps: 1. Attempt to open a deep-linked authenticated page while the session is expired (captures SESSION_TIMEOUT_REDIRECT_URL)
expected_results: handleSessionTimeoutRedirect reads and clears AuthUser::SESSION_TIMEOUT_REDIRECT_URL and ValidateController redirects there instead of the default home page, provided it differs from the login/logout URLs.

testcase_name: Public authentication pages remain reachable without a session
test_objective: Verify login, forgot-password and reset-password pages are excluded from the session-expiry enforcement.
test_steps: 1. With no active session, navigate to /auth/login, /auth/requestPasswordResetCode, and a valid /auth/resetPassword/resetCode/{code} link
expected_results: Each controller implements PublicControllerInterface; AuthenticationSubscriber::onControllerEvent returns early for these routes without throwing SessionExpiredException.

testcase_name: Unauthenticated request to a protected page never exposes protected content
test_objective: Verify an unauthenticated user hitting a non-public controller is always intercepted before any business content renders.
test_steps: 1. With no session/cookies, navigate directly to a known authenticated-only URL
expected_results: onRequestEvent stops propagation since isAuthenticated() is false, and onControllerEvent subsequently throws SessionExpiredException (or 401 for REST), so protected data is never rendered.

testcase_name: Login attempt with a disabled user account and correct password
test_objective: Verify a disabled account cannot log in even when the password is correct, and receives a specific message.
test_steps: 2. Enter the username of a disabled account
expected_results: setCredentialsForUser detects !$user->getStatus() and throws AuthenticationException::userDisabled ('Account disabled'); login is refused.

testcase_name: Login attempt with a terminated employee's user account
test_objective: Verify an account belonging to a terminated employee cannot log in even with correct credentials.
test_steps: 2. Enter the username tied to a terminated employee
expected_results: setCredentialsForUser detects an EmployeeTerminationRecord and throws AuthenticationException::employeeTerminated ('Employee is terminated'); login is refused.

testcase_name: Login attempt with a user account that has no linked employee
test_objective: Verify a system user account without an associated employee record cannot complete login.
test_steps: 2. Enter the username of a user with empNumber = null
expected_results: setCredentialsForUser throws AuthenticationException::employeeNotAssigned ('Employee not assigned'); login is refused.

testcase_name: Login attempt with a deleted user account
test_objective: Verify a soft-deleted user account is rejected with the generic invalid-credentials message rather than a specific status message.
test_steps: 2. Enter the username of a user where isDeleted()=true
expected_results: setCredentialsForUser returns false immediately for a deleted user (no specific exception), so AuthProviderChain reports failure and ValidateController shows the generic invalid_credentials message - distinct from the disabled/terminated messaging.

testcase_name: Forced password-save flows reject disabled/terminated users at the final save step
test_objective: Verify that even if a reset/enforce-password code is otherwise valid, the underlying save is blocked for a disabled or terminated account.
test_steps: 1. Obtain a valid reset-password or enforce-password reset code for a user
2. Disable the user's account or terminate their employee record before completing the reset
expected_results: ResetPasswordService::validateUser / PasswordStrengthService's user validation reject the account (returns null for a terminated employee), so saveResetPassword/saveEnforcedPassword does not update the credentials.

testcase_name: Previously issued reset links become unusable once the account is disabled mid-flow
test_objective: Verify a reset code requested while the account was active cannot be exploited after the account is disabled before the code is used.
test_steps: 1. Request a password reset for an active account (obtain code)
2. Disable the account before the code is used
3. Attempt to complete the reset using the code
expected_results: validateUser in ResetPasswordService checks the employee's termination status at save time; combined with searchForUserRecord's status checks at request time, a disabled account cannot have its password changed via a stale link.

testcase_name: No lockout after repeated failed login attempts
test_objective: Document current behaviour: verify whether the application locks or throttles an account after multiple consecutive failed login attempts.

2. Attempt login again with the correct password
expected_results: No brute-force lockout, delay, or CAPTCHA mechanism was found in LocalAuthProvider/AuthenticationService/ValidateController; the correct-password attempt succeeds immediately afterward, confirming no rate limiting is currently implemented (gap, not a verified protection).

testcase_name: Error messages differentiate account-status reasons but not username validity
test_objective: Verify that while wrong-password and unknown-username both return a generic message, disabled/terminated/unassigned states return distinct messages that could allow limited account-status enumeration.

3. Attempt login against a known-terminated-employee username with any password
expected_results: Steps 1 uses the generic 'invalid_credentials' message, while steps 2 and 3 return distinct 'user_disabled' / 'employee_terminated' messages - confirming an attacker could infer that a disabled/terminated username exists, unlike a wrong password or unknown username.

testcase_name: Create text post with valid text
test_objective: Verify user can create a text-only Buzz post with valid content.
test_steps: 3. Enter valid text in post box (e.g. Happy Friday everyone)
expected_results: Post is created successfully and appears at the top of the Buzz feed with entered text, author name, and timestamp.

testcase_name: Create text post with empty text
test_objective: Verify system rejects a text post submitted without any text.

testcase_name: Create text post with text at max boundary length (65530 chars)
test_objective: Verify a text post with text exactly at the 65530 character maximum length is accepted.
expected_results: Post is created successfully without truncation or error.

testcase_name: Create text post exceeding max length (65531 chars)
test_objective: Verify system rejects text post content exceeding the 65530 character limit.
expected_results: Validation error is shown and post is not created.

testcase_name: Create post with invalid type value
test_objective: Verify system rejects a post submitted with a type value outside of text, photo, and video.

testcase_name: Create text post with special characters and emoji
